transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. How can I help you today?

Well, doc, it's... it's kind of embarrassing, honestly, but it's getting to be a real hassle. I mean, I work in HR, so I'm used to dealing with people's problems all day, smoothing things over, figuring out schedules and logistics and all that. But lately, I find myself spending half my morning just... just trying to figure out how to get from point A to point B without having to go over any of those high bridges. You know the ones, where you can see the water way, way down below? Just thinking about them makes my stomach do flips. 

So, what brings me in is I keep planning my days around not having to drive over those high bridges. I'll take the long way, I'll sit in traffic on the surface streets for an extra forty-five minutes, whatever it takes. And look, sometimes... sometimes you just can't avoid it. Sometimes there's an accident on the other route, or I'm running late for a meeting, and I just have to do it. And when that happens, if I can't get around it, I white-knuckle it the whole way. I mean, both hands gripping the steering wheel so hard my fingers ache, staring straight ahead, heart pounding... it's just exhausting. I can't keep doing this every time I need to cross town.
When you're not driving over high bridges, do you experience similar anxiety in other situations—like being in crowded places, social settings, or open spaces?

No, no, nothing like that. It’s actually kind of funny you ask that, because my wife was wondering the exact same thing a while back. But no, crowds and social things? Totally fine. I mean, like I was saying, I work in HR. If I couldn't handle social settings or being around a lot of people, I'd have been out of a job twenty years ago! I'm constantly talking to people, running new hire orientations, standing up in front of rooms full of people, mediating disputes between employees who can't stand each other... you know how it gets in a busy office. So being around people, even large groups or packed rooms, that doesn't bother me one bit. I'm completely comfortable with all of that. 

And as for crowded places outside of work, like the mall or a stadium? Also totally fine. I go to baseball games, elbow-to-elbow with thousands of screaming fans, waiting in those huge packed lines just to get a hot dog, and my heart rate doesn't even tick up. Same goes for open spaces. I love going out to the park, just walking around the big open fields, no issues at all. 

It's really just... it's just those high bridges. It's so specific, you know? Like, put me on solid ground in the middle of a packed concert, I'm happy as a clam. Put me in a car on a flat, normal highway with a million other cars around me, perfectly fine. But the second the ground drops away underneath the road and I'm suspended way up there over the water... that's when the panic hits me. But yeah, everywhere else? Groceries, meetings, wide open spaces? Not a single problem. I've never felt that kind of stomach-dropping fear anywhere except when I'm up high on one of those spans.

The phobia is isolated to high bridges, which does not meet criteria for agoraphobia, social phobia, or other anxiety disorders, pointing toward a specific phobia under F40.29.
